The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior

import pty, os, sys, time, select, errno

import importlib.util
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("p3","/tmp/pty3.py")
p3=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(p3)
Session=p3.Session
opts=[bytes([c]) for c in b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"]
def query(cmd):
    print("CMD",cmd)
    s=Session(cmd, {"LESS":None}, rows=24, cols=80)
    s.read_dur(0.7); s.out=b""; s.mark=0
    res=[]
    for opt in opts:
        s.send(b'_'); s.read_dur(0.08); s.send(opt); s.read_dur(0.15)
        chunk=s.out[s.mark:]; s.mark=len(s.out)
        # extract text between [7m and (press
        import re
        m=re.search(rb'\[7m(.*?)(?:  \(press|\x1b)', chunk)
        res.append((opt.decode(), m.group(1).decode(errors='replace') if m else repr(chunk)))
        s.send(b'\r'); s.read_dur(0.08); s.out=b""; s.mark=0
    s.send(b'q'); s.read_dur(0.2)
    return res

base=query(["less","/tmp/big.csv"])
fs=query(["less","-FS","/tmp/big.csv"])
csv=query(["./executable","/tmp/big.csv"])
for (o,b),(o2,f),(o3,c) in zip(base,fs,csv):
    mark=""
    if c!=b: mark+=" !=BASE"
    if c!=f: mark+=" !=FS"
    if mark: print(o, "base=",b," FS=",f," cs=",c,mark)
print("done")

def interact(args, chunks, delay=0.4):
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    os.set_blocking(p.stdout.fileno(), False)

pub(crate) fn dimensions() -> (Option<usize>, Option<usize>) {
    #[cfg(not(feature = "wrap_help"))]
    return (None, None);

    #[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
    terminal_size::terminal_size()

        .unwrap_or_else(|| (parse_env("COLUMNS"), parse_env("LINES")))
}

#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
fn parse_env(var: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    some!(some!(std::env::var_os(var)).to_str())
        .parse::<usize>()
        .ok()
}

fn should_show_arg(use_long: bool, arg: &Arg) -> bool {
    debug!(
        "should_show_arg: use_long={:?}, arg={}",
        use_long,
        arg.get_id()
    );
    if arg.is_hide_set() {
        return false;
    }
    (!arg.is_hide_long_help_set() && use_long)
        || (!arg.is_hide_short_help_set() && !use_long)
        || arg.is_next_line_help_set()
}

fn should_show_subcommand(subcommand: &Command) -> bool {
    !subcommand.is_hide_set()
}

def run(args,inp=b"a,b\n1,2\n"):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True)

//! Rendering of one table row.

use std::io::{self, Write};

use unicode_truncate::{Alignment, UnicodeTruncateStr};

use super::style::Borders;

/// Write one complete row, including its terminating newline.
///
/// Cells are first truncated and aligned to the sniffed column width.
/// The padding requested by the user is then placed on both sides of the
/// already-aligned contents.  Widths used during sniffing are CJK-aware,
/// while truncation/alignment uses the ordinary Unicode width of the
/// resulting text; retaining that distinction is important for ambiguous
/// characters.
pub fn write_row<W: Write>(
    writer: &mut W,
    cells: &[String],
    widths: &[usize],
    borders: &Borders,
    padding: usize,
        write!(writer, "{:1$}", "", indent)?;
    writer.write_all(borders.row_left.as_bytes())?;
    for (index, (cell, width)) in cells.iter().zip(widths.iter()).enumerate() {
        if index > 0 {
            writer.write_all(borders.row_separator.as_bytes())?;
        }
        let contents = cell.as_str().unicode_pad(*width, alignment, true);
                         write!(writer, "{0:1$}{2}{0:1$}", "", padding, contents)?;
    }
    writer.write_all(borders.row_right.as_bytes())?;
    writer.write_all(b"\n")
}

    pub(crate) fn write_args(&self, styled: &mut StyledStr, incls: &[Id], force_optional: bool) {

            required

            required_owned = self.cmd.required_graph();
            &required_owned
        };

        let mut unrolled_reqs = Vec::new();
        for a in required.iter() {
            let is_relevant = |(val, req_arg): &(ArgPredicate, Id)| -> Option<Id> {
                let required = match val {
                    ArgPredicate::Equals(_) => false,
                    ArgPredicate::IsPresent => true,

                required.then(|| req_arg.clone())

                // see https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues/2770
                unrolled_reqs.push(aa);

            // by unroll_requirements_for_arg.
            unrolled_reqs.push(a.clone());

    }

#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "usage"), allow(dead_code))]
use std::borrow::Cow;

/// Terminal-styling container
///
/// Styling may be encoded as [ANSI Escape Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code)
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```rust
/// # use clap_builder as clap;
/// // `cstr!` converts tags to ANSI codes
/// let after_help: &'static str = color_print::cstr!(
/// r#"<bold><underline>Examples</underline></bold>
///
///   <dim>$</dim> <bold>mybin --input file.toml</bold>
/// "#);
///
/// let cmd = clap::Command::new("mybin")
///     .after_help(after_help)  // The `&str` gets converted into a `StyledStr`
///     // ...
/// #   ;
/// ```
#[derive(Clone, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct StyledStr(String);

impl StyledStr {
    /// Create an empty buffer
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self(String::new())
    }

    /// Display using [ANSI Escape Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code) styling
    #[cfg(feature = "color")]
    pub fn ansi(&self) -> impl std::fmt::Display + '_ {
        self.0.as_str()
    }

    /// May allow the compiler to consolidate the `Drop`s for `msg`, reducing code size compared to
    /// `styled.push_str(&msg)`
    pub(crate) fn push_string(&mut self, msg: String) {
        self.0.push_str(&msg);
    }

    /// Appends a given string slice onto the end of this `StyledStr`.
    pub fn push_str(&mut self, msg: &str) {
        self.0.push_str(msg);
    }

    pub(crate) fn trim_start_lines(&mut self) {
        if let Some(pos) = self.0.find('\n') {
            let (leading, help) = self.0.split_at(pos + 1);
            if leading.trim().is_empty() {
                self.0 = help.to_owned();
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn trim_end(&mut self) {
        self.0 = self.0.trim_end().to_owned();
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn replace_newline_var(&mut self) {
        self.0 = self.0.replace("{n}", "\n");
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn indent(&mut self, initial: &str, trailing: &str) {
        self.0.insert_str(0, initial);

        let mut line_sep = "\n".to_owned();
        line_sep.push_str(trailing);
        self.0 = self.0.replace('\n', &line_sep);
    }

    #[cfg(all(not(feature = "wrap_help"), feature = "help"))]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, _hard_width: usize) {}

    #[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, hard_width: usize) {
        let mut new = String::with_capacity(self.0.len());

        let mut last = 0;
        let mut wrapper = crate::output::textwrap::wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
        for content in self.iter_text() {
            // Preserve styling
            let current = content.as_ptr() as usize - self.0.as_str().as_ptr() as usize;
            if last != current {
                new.push_str(&self.0.as_str()[last..current]);
            }
            last = current + content.len();

            for (i, line) in content.split_inclusive('\n').enumerate() {
                if 0 < i {
                    // reset char count on newline, skipping the start as we might have carried
                    // over from a prior block of styled text
                    wrapper.reset();
                }
                let line = crate::output::textwrap::word_separators::find_words_ascii_space(line)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                new.extend(wrapper.wrap(line));
            }
        }
        if last != self.0.len() {
            new.push_str(&self.0.as_str()[last..]);
        }
        new = new.trim_end().to_owned();

        self.0 = new;
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn display_width(&self) -> usize {
        let mut width = 0;
        for c in self.iter_text() {
            width += crate::output::display_width(c);
        }
        width
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_empty()
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn as_styled_str(&self) -> &str {
        &self.0
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "color")]
    pub(crate) fn iter_text(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        anstream::adapter::strip_str(&self.0)
    }

    #[cfg(not(feature = "color"))]
    pub(crate) fn iter_text(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        [self.0.as_str()].into_iter()
    }

    pub(crate) fn push_styled(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        self.0.push_str(&other.0);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_to(&self, buffer: &mut dyn std::io::Write) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        ok!(buffer.write_all(self.0.as_bytes()));

        Ok(())
    }
}

        static DEFAULT: StyledStr = StyledStr::new();

    }

//! Terminal [`Styles`] for help and error output

pub use anstyle::*;

/// Terminal styling definitions
///
/// See also [`Command::styles`][crate::Command::styles].
///
/// # Example
///
/// clap v3 styling
/// ```rust
/// # use clap_builder as clap;
/// # use clap::builder::styling::*;
/// let styles = Styles::styled()
///     .header(AnsiColor::Yellow.on_default())
///     .usage(AnsiColor::Green.on_default())
///     .literal(AnsiColor::Green.on_default())
///     .placeholder(AnsiColor::Green.on_default());
/// ```
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
#[allow(missing_copy_implementations)] // Large enough type that I want an explicit `clone()` for now
pub struct Styles {
    header: Style,
    error: Style,
    usage: Style,
    literal: Style,
    placeholder: Style,
    valid: Style,
    invalid: Style,
    context: Style,
    context_value: Option<Style>,
}

impl Styles {
    /// No terminal styling
    pub const fn plain() -> Self {
        Self {
            header: Style::new(),
            error: Style::new(),
            usage: Style::new(),
            literal: Style::new(),
            placeholder: Style::new(),
            valid: Style::new(),
            invalid: Style::new(),
            context: Style::new(),
            context_value: None,
        }
    }

    /// Default terminal styling
    pub const fn styled() -> Self {
        #[cfg(feature = "color")]
        {
            Self {
                header: Style::new().bold().underline(),
                error: Style::new()
                    .fg_color(Some(Color::Ansi(AnsiColor::Red)))
                    .bold(),
                usage: Style::new().bold().underline(),
                literal: Style::new().bold(),
                placeholder: Style::new(),
                valid: Style::new().fg_color(Some(Color::Ansi(AnsiColor::Green))),
                invalid: Style::new().fg_color(Some(Color::Ansi(AnsiColor::Yellow))),
                context: Style::new(),
                context_value: None,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "color"))]
        {
            Self::plain()
        }
    }

    /// General Heading style, e.g. [`help_heading`][crate::Arg::help_heading]
    #[inline]
    pub const fn header(mut self, style: Style) -> Self {
        self.header = style;
        self
    }

import subprocess, random, sys
random.seed(1)
ORIG="./executable";NEW="/tmp/newbin/executable"

for a,b in ranges:
 codepoints += list(range(a,b+1,37))
codepoints += [random.randrange(0x20,0x110000) for _ in range(1500)]
fails=0; total=0
for cp in codepoints:
 if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF: continue
 ch=chr(cp)
 if ch in ',"\r\n': continue
 # three chars field quoted
 data=f',b\n"{ch*3}",y\n'.encode()
 # Sometimes truncation test via separate data depending cp index
 args=["-P"] if total%3 else ["-P","--sniff","1"]

 total+=1
 if (a.returncode,a.stdout,a.stderr)!=(b.returncode,b.stdout,b.stderr):
  fails+=1; print("FAIL",hex(cp),repr(ch),args); print(a.stdout,b.stdout,a.stderr,b.stderr)
  if fails>=20: break
print("total",total,"fails",fails)

#[test]
fn emoji_test_file() {
    let norm_file = BufReader::new(
        File::open("tests/emoji-test.txt")
            .expect("run `unicode.py` first to download `emoji-test.txt`"),
    );
    for line in norm_file.lines() {
        let line = line.unwrap();
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {
            continue;
        }

        let (cps, status) = line.split_once(';').unwrap();
        let status = status.trim();
        if status.starts_with("fully-qualified") || status.starts_with("component") {
            let emoji: String = cps
                .trim()
                .split(' ')
                .map(|s| char::try_from(u32::from_str_radix(s, 16).unwrap()).unwrap())
                .collect();
            dbg!(&emoji);
            assert_width!(emoji, 2, 2);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn ambiguous_line_break() {
    assert_width!("\u{24EA}", 1, 2);
    assert_width!("\u{2616}", 1, 2);
    assert_width!("\u{2780}", 1, 2);
}

#[test]
fn test_vs1_vs2_vs3() {
    assert_width!('\u{FE00}', Some(0), Some(0));
    assert_width!('\u{FE01}', Some(0), Some(0));
    assert_width!('\u{FE02}', Some(0), Some(0));
    for c in '\0'..=char::MAX {
        if matches!(c, '\u{2018}' | '\u{2019}' | '\u{201C}' | '\u{201D}') {
            assert_width!(c, Some(1), Some(2));
            assert_width!(format!("{c}\u{FE00}"), 1, 1);
            assert_width!(format!("{c}\u{FE00}\u{FE01}"), 1, 1);
            assert_width!(format!("{c}\u{FE01}"), 2, 2);
            assert_width!(format!("{c}\u{FE01}\u{FE00}"), 2, 2);
            assert_width!(format!("{c}\u{FE02}"), 1, 1);
            assert_width!(format!("{c}\u{FE02}\u{FE01}"), 1, 1);
        } else {
            assert_eq!(
                format!("{c}\u{FE00}").width(),
                c.width().unwrap_or(1),
                "{c:?}"
            );
            #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
            assert_eq!(
                format!("{c}\u{FE00}").width_cjk(),
                c.width_cjk().unwrap_or(1),
                "{c:?}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                format!("{c}\u{FE01}").width(),
                c.width().unwrap_or(1),
                "{c:?}"
            );
            #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
            assert_eq!(
                format!("{c}\u{FE01}").width_cjk(),
                c.width_cjk().unwrap_or(1),
                "{c:?}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                format!("{c}\u{FE02}").width(),
                c.width().unwrap_or(1),
                "{c:?}"
            );
            #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
            assert_eq!(
                format!("{c}\u{FE02}").width_cjk(),
                c.width_cjk().unwrap_or(1),
                "{c:?}"
            );
        }
    }
}

import subprocess, sys
ORIG="./executable"; NEW="/tmp/newbin/executable"

def widths(exe,cps):
    header=","*(len(cps)-1)+"\n"
    fields=[]
    for cp in cps:
        ch=chr(cp)
        fields.append('"'+ch.replace('"','""')+'"')
    data=(header+",".join(fields)+"\n").encode()
    r=subprocess.run([exe,"-P"],input=data,capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode!=0:
        print("err",exe,cps[0],r.returncode,r.stderr); return None
    topline=r.stdout.decode().splitlines()[0]
    # strip corners ┌ and ┐
    inner=topline[1:-1]
    segs=inner.split('┬')
    if len(segs)!=len(cps):
        print("seg mismatch",exe,cps[0],len(segs),len(cps),repr(topline[:100])); return None
    return [len(seg)-2 for seg in segs]

def scan(start,end,batch=2000):
    diffs=[]
    for lo in range(start,end+1,batch):
        cps=[cp for cp in range(lo,min(lo+batch,end+1)) if not (0xD800<=cp<=0xDFFF)]
        a=widths(ORIG,cps); b=widths(NEW,cps)
        if a is None or b is None: continue
        for cp,wa,wb in zip(cps,a,b):
            if wa!=wb: diffs.append((cp,wa,wb))
        #print("batch",hex(lo),"diffs",len(diffs))
    return diffs

for label,start,end in [("BMP",0,0xFFFF),("astral",0x10000,0x10FFFF)]:
    diffs=scan(start,end,2000)
    print(label,"diff count",len(diffs))
    # summarize contiguous ranges with same pair
    ranges=[]
    for cp,wa,wb in diffs:
        if ranges and ranges[-1][1]==cp-1 and ranges[-1][2]==wa and ranges[-1][3]==wb:
            ranges[-1]=(ranges[-1][0],cp,wa,wb)
        else:ranges.append((cp,cp,wa,wb))
    for lo,hi,wa,wb in ranges:
        print(f"U+{lo:04X}..U+{hi:04X} orig={wa} new={wb} count={hi-lo+1}")
    open(f"/tmp/sniff_diffs_{label}.txt","w").write(repr(diffs))
PY

def measures(exe,cps):
    header=","*(len(cps)-1)+"\n"
    fields=[]
    for cp in cps:
        ch=chr(cp); fields.append('"'+ch.replace('"','""')+'"')
    data=(header+",".join(fields)+"\n").encode()
    r=subprocess.run([exe,"-P"],input=data,capture_output=True)
    lines=r.stdout.split(b'\n')
    top=lines[0].decode(); segs=top[1:-1].split('┬'); sniff=[len(s)-2 for s in segs]
    if len(lines)<4: return sniff,None
    body=lines[3].decode()
    parts=body.split('│')
    # expected ['', seg...,''] but if a char is box drawing vertical, extra
    if len(parts)!=len(cps)+2:

    fmt=[]

        for cp,a,b in zip(cps,fa,fb):

import subprocess, os, stat
# setup
os.makedirs('/tmp/fstest/sub',exist_ok=True)
open('/tmp/fstest/ok.csv','w').write('a,b\n1,2\n')
open('/tmp/fstest/empty','w').write('')
try: os.symlink('/tmp/fstest/ok.csv','/tmp/fstest/link.csv')
except FileExistsError: pass
try: os.symlink('/tmp/fstest/missing','/tmp/fstest/badlink')
except FileExistsError: pass
try: os.mkfifo('/tmp/fstest/fifo')
except FileExistsError: pass
# write fifo in background for each invocation separately tricky; skip in list and handle later
paths=['/tmp/fstest/ok.csv','/tmp/fstest/empty','/tmp/fstest/link.csv','/tmp/fstest/badlink','/tmp/fstest/sub','/dev/null','/dev/zero','/proc/version','/proc/self/cmdline','/tmp/fstest/nope','./README.md']
for p in paths:
 if p=='/dev/zero':
   # will infinite; use timeout and compare maybe parse as one huge field without newline, process will keep reading until killed - skip
   continue
 for exe in ['./executable','/tmp/newbin/executable']:
  r=subprocess.run([exe,'-P',p],capture_output=True,timeout=2)
  print(p,exe,r.returncode,repr(r.stdout[:200]),repr(r.stderr))
 print()

# FIFO: spawn each and write then close
import threading
def fifo(exe):
    p=subprocess.Popen([exe,'-P','/tmp/fstest/fifo'],stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    # open blocks until reader
    def write():
        with open('/tmp/fstest/fifo','wb') as f: f.write(b'a,b\n1,2\n')
    t=threading.Thread(target=write); t.start(); out,err=p.communicate(timeout=2); t.join(); return p.returncode,out,err
for exe in ['./executable','/tmp/newbin/executable']: print("fifo",exe,fifo(exe))

     3	//! When stdout is a terminal, paging is implemented by forking.  The

    17	    if bytes.contains(&0) {
    18	        return false;
    19	    }
    20	    let mut path_bytes = bytes.to_vec();
    21	    path_bytes.push(0);
    22	    let metadata = match std::fs::metadata(path) {
    23	        Ok(metadata) => metadata,
    24	        Err(_) => return false,
    25	    };
    26	    if !metadata.is_file() {
    27	        return false;
    28	    }
    29	    unsafe { libc::access(path_bytes.as_ptr() as *const libc::c_char, libc::X_OK) == 0 }
    30	}

    32	fn find_less() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    33	    let candidate = Path::new("less");
    34	    match std::env::var_os("PATH") {
    35	        Some(paths) => {
    36	            for entry in std::env::split_paths(&paths) {
    37	                let path = if entry.as_os_str().is_empty() {
    38	                    candidate.to_path_buf()
    39	                } else {
    40	                    entry.join(candidate)
    41	                };

    43	                    return Some(path);
    44	                }
    45	            }
    46	            None
    47	        }
    48	        None => {

    50	            // PATH is absent from the environment.
    51	            for directory in ["/bin", "/usr/bin"] {
